image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a wet, rocky substrate. The organism displays an oval shape with a distinct dorsal armor consisting of overlapping plates embedded in a textured, leathery girdle. The surface appears wet and granular, consistent with an intertidal environment.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior end of the organism is visible and lacks any protruding sensory structures like eyes or tentacles, matching the biological description of a chiton.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the animal blends smoothly into the surrounding girdle without a defined head shape, appearing blunt as expected.
No antennae, eyestalks, or other sensory appendages are visible on the dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates are surrounded by a thick, textured mantle (girdle) that appears leathery and granular, fitting the description.
